name: How to Achieve a Smooth and Lasting Interior Paint Finish

step.name: Step 1: Protect Your Space and Clean Surfaces
step.text: First things first: protect your floors and furnishings with drop cloths and painter's tape. Then, give your walls a good cleaning. You want the surface to be sound, clean, dry, and free of any grease or contamination. A degreaser might be necessary for kitchen walls. Dust and grime can prevent paint from adhering properly, leading to an uneven finish.

step.name: Step 2: Repair and Sand Imperfections
step.text: Now's the time to fill any cracks or holes with spackle or joint compound. Repair any damaged areas, and once dry, sand them smooth. You might also need to sand existing glossy surfaces lightly to give the new paint something to grip. After sanding, wipe away all dust thoroughly. This step is crucial for a truly smooth final appearance.

step.name: Step 3: Prime When Necessary
step.text: Don't skip priming! Bare drywall, repaired patches, stained areas, or surfaces with a significant color change benefit greatly from primer. Primer creates a uniform surface, blocks stains, and helps the topcoat adhere better and achieve its true color in fewer coats. Ensure the primer is fully dry according to manufacturer instructions before moving on.

step.name: Step 4: Apply Finish Coats Evenly
step.text: Once your walls are prepped and primed, it's time for the finish coats. Apply paint in thin, even layers. Avoid overloading your brush or roller to prevent drips and runs. Pay attention to drying and recoat times as per the product label; recoating too soon can cause issues. Most rooms will need two coats for full coverage and durability.
